newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds slipped further to finish weakly in very thin trade on Monday, with the market still hungover after various Bundesbankers apparently conflicting comments on German rates on Friday, traders said.
"The market's quite wary after Tietmeyer's remarks, particularly, and it is very quiet," one dealer said.
BUBA president Tietmeyer said on Friday he saw no need for easier interest rate policy in the foreseeable future.
With no prevailing view on the direction of the market, investors were happy to sit on the sidelines waiting for some defining event, one broker said.
"We've got really low volumes and it's just getting worse," he said.
"In my view there won't be anything much happening until after the U.S. elections and the run-up to the year end."
The Dutch yield curve again saw some flattening, with the 5-10 year spread pulling in to around 100 basis points from around 103 on Friday.
Trading was largely concentrated on the 5 and 10 year maturities, although the February 2003 also saw some action, dealers said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
